title: Tariffs Don't Cause Inflation; They're Worse
summary: Tax Foundation economist: tariffs are an excise tax that cuts real income; whether the price level rises once depends on Fed accommodation, not the tariff.

assertions.quote: Accommodation would result in a one-time increase in the price level.

verdicts.note: A tariff shifts relative prices and the level once; persistent inflation requires monetary accommodation or de-anchored expectations, which the 2018-19 episode did not show.

assertions.quote: whether they affect the overall price level depends on how the Fed responds

verdicts.note: The paper identifies relative price effects with time fixed effects and explicitly holds the monetary-policy response and other general equilibrium forces fixed, leaving their quantification to future work, so it cannot say how the Fed's response changes the aggregate price-level outcome.

assertions.quote: In both cases, real incomes fall.
firms have to adjust their compensation costs by laying off workers or reducing hiring

verdicts.note: Downward nominal wage rigidity is well documented, so a real-income cut that is not absorbed by prices shows up in hiring and employment.
